html:
The Bora are a people of the Amazon forest on the border of Peru and Colombia, first between the Caquetá and Putumayo rivers. They speak a Boran language, which uses tone so strongly that it can be beaten out on large wooden signal drums called manguaré.

Around 1900 their homeland fell under the rubber company of Julio César Arana, later the Peruvian Amazon Company. Its agents forced Bora and Huitoto people to gather rubber through terror, flogging and killing. Tens of thousands died in the Putumayo atrocities, exposed in 1912 by the British consul Roger Casement.

Many survivors were moved south to the Ampiyacu River in Peru, where most Bora now live, near the Yagua.
